To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SP1 was detected in 19 out (38%) of the 50 cases of colon cancer studied and in one out (25%) of the four cases of ulcerative colonitis.

1) SP1 was detected neither in the mucosa nor in the transitional mucosa and in adenomas; 2) in 19 (38%) cases out of 50, SP1 was revealed in the epithelum and stromal macro-phages of carcinoma; 3) SP1-positive cells are located mainly in the areas of tumor invasion; 4) SP1 is a marker of colon cancer.
the expression of pregnancy-specific β1-globulin in cancer and in noncancerous colon mucosa was studied by the method of immunohistochemistry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new immunohistochemical method for the diagnosis of colorectal carcinoma.
the immunohistochemical detection of pregnancy-specific beta 1-glycoprotein (SP1) in cancer of the large intestine and in noncancerous mucosa of the colon.
the immunohistochemical analysis of trophoblastic beta-1-glycoprotein expression in cancer and the colon mucosa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SP1 is a marker of malignant transformation in the colon and rectum.
SP1 is a marker of the invasive process of the colon cancer.
SP1 is not a marker of colon cancer but a marker of the invasive stage of colon cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immunohistochemical analysis of SP1 in the colon mucosa is an important diagnostic method for cancer.
SP1 is a marker of the malignant transformation of the colon mucosa and that its detection in the tissue of the tumor is a marker of its invasive activity.
the expression of SP1 is a marker of the invasive growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SP1 protein is a tumor marker suitable for the diagnosis of colon cancer.
the presence of SP1 is a marker of tumor invasion and is a good predictor of tumor metastasis.
SP1 is a tumor marker that can be used for the diagnosis of colon cancer, as well as a prognostic factor.
